Headteacher’s Welcome
Welcome to Riverside School, a proud and ambitious community where every student is enabled to achieve, belong and thrive. Riverside is a school with high expectations and a relentless commitment to excellence for all. We challenge our students to be curious, resilient, deep-thinking and collaborative learners, to ensure that every young person leaves us with the knowledge, skills and confidence to succeed. We are committed to providing an exceptional education through high-quality inclusive teaching and learning, a broad and enriching curriculum, and excellent pastoral care. Our students are challenged to aim high, develop their talents and make a highly positive contribution to the world around them. Whether through academic success, sporting achievement, the performing arts, leadership opportunities, we celebrate the unique talents and contributions of every student.
As a truly inclusive school, we are proud of the diversity of our community and the strong relationships that underpin everything we do. We work closely with families, recognising that a successful partnership between home and school is key to helping young people flourish.
We are proud of our school, our students and our community, and look forward to welcoming you to Riverside.

Ethos & Values
The School Council have produced the following list of values which they feel are at the heart of Riverside School:
At the Riverside School, we uphold the traditional values of strong discipline, high expectations and a demanding academic curriculum. At the same time we are totally committed to the best use of 21st century computer technology to help teaching and learning. Our first priority is the development of every students’ academic potential to the fullest.
We demand that the students at Riverside achieve the very best that they are capable of, but we also work to ensure that they are happy and feel secure at school. Learning can be difficult and challenging at times, and it is our job, with the support of parents, to keep the pressure on and maintain motivation.
We believe in firm discipline: without good order in the classroom teachers cannot teach and students cannot learn. At Riverside School we do not tolerate any student who wants to stop others from learning. We expect students to take pride in belonging to their school by wearing correct school uniform and wearing it smartly and properly.
We also expect students to get involved in the wider life of the school: to join clubs, get involved in sports teams and take part in school productions. In short, to take advantage of all the opportunities that an exciting school like Riverside offers.
Modern British Values
Modern British Values are taught in every aspect of school life at Riverside: in the classroom, through our guest speakers, on the sports field and in daily interactions between staff and students. History
Riverside School serves the local community with the very highest standard of education to ensure ‘Excellence for All’. Riverside works in partnership with the Local Authority (London Borough of Barking & Dagenham) to meet the needs of a rapidly growing school population in the Thames View and Riverside areas in the south of the Borough, adjoining the Thames. At Riverside School, we uphold the traditional values of strong discipline, school uniform and a demanding classroom ethos. We demand that the children at Riverside achieve the very best that they are capable of, but we also work to ensure that they are happy and feel secure at school.
Learning can be difficult and challenging at times, and it is our job, with the support of parents, to keep the pressure on and maintain motivation. We believe in firm discipline: without good order in the classroom teachers cannot teach and students cannot learn. At Riverside School we do not tolerate any student who wants to stop others from learning. We expect students to take a pride in belonging to their school by wearing correct school uniform and wearing it smartly and properly. We also expect students to get involved in the wider life of the school: to join clubs, get involved in sports teams and take part in school productions.
In September 2017 we moved into our purpose built £45 million building which also accommodates Riverside Primary School and Riverside Bridge School (special school) on one campus. The collaboration and joint planning of all three schools affords students opportunities to move seamlessly between schools for a range of learning experiences. Riverside School is one of the founding schools in the Partnership Learning Teaching School Alliance which is a network of schools that serve the East London boroughs of Barking & Dagenham and Havering.
Riverside School plays an integral leading role in the Alliance, helping to source and support the recruitment of new and high quality teachers into the profession. Our success is a result of an absolute emphasis on learning, the brilliant parental support that we receive and our close-knit team of enthusiastic and incredibly talented staff. There is a real sense of passion and dynamism that students and staff bring to all that they do, making Riverside school a superb place to both learn and to work.

SEND Policies
As with all our students, students with Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND) are valued members of the school community and make a strong contribution to its success. Riverside School complies with the “Special Educational Needs and Disability Code of Practice: 0 to 25 years” June 2014 (updated May 2015). Our policy outlined below shows the action we take to provide a secure and positive environment for students with SEND, in which all can achieve well and be successful. Our policy describes the responsibilities of our staff and the partnership we seek to establish with parents in providing a positive transition to secondary education and a successful school experience for children with SEND, whether or not they have an Educational Health and Care Plan (EHCP)
If you have any enquiries relating to the Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND) provision at Riverside School that you wish to be addressed, please contact Mrs Del Rio (the Special Educational Needs Coordinator) by using our contact page here.

Curriculum
Riverside School works closely with four other local sixth forms, which allows students a wider range of choice when looking at what subjects they want to study. Subjects may be based in any of the other four schools in our partnership, which are:
Most students will be doing 3 linear A-Level courses that will be picked from each of the 4 blocks displayed below. The precise make up of each student’s courses and timetable will be finally decided in light of GCSE results and in discussion with the Director of Sixth Form.
To start A-Level courses, students will need the appropriate Attainment 8 score from their GCSEs including grade 5 for both GCSE English and Maths (students with grade 4 will also be considered but their course choice will be more limited). If the A-Level is a subject taken at GCSE the student should have a 6 or more in that subject.
For Maths A-Level, students will need a 6 in the higher tier GCSE and also pass the entry exam. Science students will also need Maths GCSE 5 plus a grade 7-7 combined science or grade 7 in the science they wish to study.
Physics cannot be taken unless the student is also studying Maths.
Further Maths is by invitation only, based on student’s performance in A-Level Maths Exam.
Students who have completed their GCSEs at Riverside School but may not be suited to linear A-Level courses have the choice of completing the CTEC Applied Science. This requires students to have achieved a 5-5 in combined science at GCSE, and the course is the equivalent of 2 full A-levels. Students will study this along-side one A-level, and will be required to meet the entry standards outlined above.
Alternatively, students can apply to a variety of courses at the partnership schools. Level 1 courses are available at Dagenham Park School and vocational courses which include BTECs are an option at Jo Richardson School, Eastbury School and Dagenham Park School.

Independent Personal Guidance – Prospects
We have a dedicated Careers Co-ordinator in school who facilitates and promotes our Careers Programme, as well as an independent Careers Advisor (who visits the school at set times) and a member of SLT who is responsible for overseeing the Careers Provision within the school. Every member of staff is aware of the responsibility they play towards building a comprehensive and coherent careers programme and understand the value of making the careers education explicit, relevant and dynamic.
Purpose and Aims of Careers Education at Riverside School
At Riverside School we aim to provide an inclusive, effective and stable careers programme for all of our students from year 7, right through to year 13. The programme aims to raise student aspirations, broaden horizons and promote equal opportunities. We are working to develop a programme that is an integral part of the academic and wider curriculum to ensure students receive appropriate information and guidance, especially at decision and transition points. Students will develop the skills they need to take responsibility for their personal and career development. Our programme will be tailored to support key student groups to ensure all students enter further or higher education, training or employment.
Delivery and guidance
Using the Gatsby Benchmarks of good career guidance, we have designed a detailed (and ever evolving) strategy that ensures all students take part in activities that help inspire and educate them, opening their eyes to the boundless career opportunities that exist in today’s ever changing landscape, and allow them to make informed career choices and decisions.

Students will also be offered bespoke opportunities throughout the school year, which may include; school trips, careers fairs, tailored civics lessons, workshops, carefully selected inspirational speakers and lifelong learning, all of which are aimed at enabling a full rounded education and experience of possible future careers.
Monitor, Review and Evaluation
The development of the careers programme has been highlighted in the school improvement plan (written in Autumn term). The actions put forward are subject to review and evaluation every term. The impact of Riverside’s career programme on the students will be evaluated and assessed through a range of different strategies which include, but are not limited to;
This information will allow us to modify and tailor our careers plan, in order to more fully meet the individual needs of our students.
We will constantly update and evaluate our programme based on the introduction of new technology, education and careers information, which will enable us to make sure that we are able to provide the most relevant, up-to-date and inclusive programme for all of our students.
Provider Access Policy
In accordance with the requirements of the statutory guidance, ‘Careers Guidance and Access for Education and Training Providers’ (October 2018) and the obligations placed upon schools by section 42B of the Education Act 1997, this policy sets out Riverside School’s arrangements for managing the access of education and training providers to pupils at the school.
Management of Provider Access Requests
A provider wishing to request access should contact Carole Spike-Robertson, CEIAG Coordinator
Phone: 0203 946 5919 or email: casp@riverside.bardaglea.org.uk
Opportunities for Access
Careers education is delivered through subject areas, in the CIVICS programme, in tutor time activities, via year group assemblies and events and key stage events, as well as whole school activities.
All subject areas have explicit links to careers in their schemes of work and in their classroom/corridor displays. Audits are undertaken to make sure that this is the case.
We work with a range of organisations from the further and higher education sector, training providers and apprenticeship providers. We also have links with a wide and evolving range of businesses in varied sectors. We bring workplace representatives into school to provide workplace relevance to our careers activities and to support our vocational teaching. We have strong relationships with businesses, both local and national, and we actively seek new relationships. We use a range of organisations, such as Speakers for Schools, Amazing Apprenticeships, BEP, Unifrog, and Prospects as well as using parent and teacher contacts.
We have also developed strong links with organisations promoting social mobility and university access, such as:
We also work with the Careers and Enterprise Company in order to develop long lasting relationships with businesses.
At Riverside School we have a dedicated careers area for all students, which is based in the main library, as well as a dedicated careers library for sixth form students, which contains a wealth of information on pathways and university application information. We also use the Unifrog Careers Platform for which all students have their own unique log in for and can add their own information to.
